newsitem.title: USA: UBS sets Cascade price target of $80.
newsitem.headline: UBS sets Cascade price target of $80.

text.p: UBS analyst Nikos Theodosopoulos said he set a minimum price target of $80 a share on Cascade Communications Corp, which he said reflected a more sober appraisal of the company following its third quarter report.
The analyst also set a target of $70 for PairGain Technologies Inc.
"Based on our valuation of these two companies, we believe the stocks will minimally appreciate to $80 for Cascade and $70 for Pairgain over the next nine months," Theodosopoulos wrote.

Both stocks have undergone sharp price corrections in recent weeks after failing to produce financial results that several Wall Street analysts have argued were necessary to justify their high trading multiples.
Monday, shares of Cascade regained some of the ground they lost Friday in a 15-point battering that followed the release of the company's third quarter earnings report.
By early afternoon Monday, the stock was up 4-1/8 to 75-1/2.
Last Tuesday, the stock had reached a record intra-day high of 91-1/4 and had closed just under 90.
PairGain stock was up four in Monday afternoon trading at 70-1/4. Last Wednesday, Pairgain shares gave up nine points to fall to 71-3/4 following its third quarter earnings report.
The analyst's office said he had not had a recent price target for Cascade, as the stock's rapid appreciation had blown through his previous price target months ago.
Theodosopoulos had put a $79 price target on Pairgain when he initiated the stock about three months ago.

The analysts' new price target on Cascade reflected the more conservative appraisal that has begun to take hold on Wall Street since Cascade's third quarter report of $0.21 per share -- $0.02 above the analysts' consensus -- but below the most aggressive expectations floated on Wall Street.
The company had reported $0.07 per share in the 1995 third quarter.

Theodosopoulos joined other analysts who have argued that the sharp sell-off reflected the company's failure to show enough "upside surprise" in its earnings results. Nonetheless, he said he believes the company's fundamentals remain secure.
The third quarter's $0.21 per share represented earnings growth of more than 200 percent year-to-year, but only 17 percent sequentially from the second quarter of this year.
Several analysts have argued that the slower sequential growth could not justify the high price/earnings multiples the stock had previously commanded.

Writing of his new price targets for both stocks, the analyst cautioned that "while these levels may or (may) not be reached, or if reached, may not represent near-term bottoms, we believe they are excellent accumulation points."
